column1: # The size of this census is pinned, and checked by parity-manifest-check.sh. Four groups are
# reconciled against a source file and every row a lane speaks for is reconciled against the
# results, but a BLOCKED row in `divergence`, `install`, `pool`, `state` or `log` is spoken for by
# nothing — and deleting one leaves the numerator alone while shrinking the denominator, so the
# reported coverage goes UP. This number is what makes that a red rather than an improvement.
# Moving it is a deliberate line in a diff, which is the point: the denominator is R4-C's cutover
# target. Add or remove a row and move the pin in the same change.
# One row per capability the cutover requires the Swift router to answer for. The gate reports
# coverage as a fraction of THIS file, so a row that is missing here does not make the gate red —
# it shrinks the denominator and the coverage number goes UP. scripts/acceptance/parity-manifest-check.sh
# derives the control and fixture rows from source and fails when this file and the source disagree,
#   group    control | fixture | divergence | mcp | cli | pool | install | state | log
#   id       stable row id; a lane reports results against it. Unique across the file.
#   subject  for control rows, the exact route string control.ts answers. For fixture rows, the
#            fixture basename. Both are checked mechanically against source.
#   owner    the item that would unblock a blocked row; "-" when not blocked
#   note     why. A blocked row's note says what is missing, not that it is missing.
# proven          a lane compared both routers on this subject and they agreed
# proven-by-suite no wire observation exists; a named test asserts it. Weaker, and printed as such
# blocked         not compared. Never counted toward coverage
# control — the 15 (path, method) pairs src/control.ts dispatches

Driven over a real socket at BOTH routers by parity-stream.sh, which existed from R2-R and which parity-gate.sh had never run: `stream` was absent from its LANES list, so the script was dispatched by nothing while this row stayed blocked under a note about SSE that R2-R had already made untrue. FOUR verdicts, because framing agreement is not body parity and neither is a frame count. (1) The response head - status line and every header, Date aside - byte-identical; nothing had ever compared a header on this route, so `cache-control: no-store` and `connection: keep-alive` were asserted nowhere. (2) The frame region compared LINE BY LINE including the blank lines that terminate each SSE frame, with an unrecognised line kind (event:, id:, retry:) a named failure even when both sides produce it - the previous form grepped for three line kinds and deleted the terminators its own comment claimed were compared byte for byte. (3) A subscriber that joins LATE receives no backlog, asserted as an absolute zero on each side BEFORE the two are diffed, because two routers that both replay diff clean; then exactly the one record driven after it joined, byte for byte. (4) Both original connections still open after the heartbeat AND the record driven afterwards compared BYTE FOR BYTE on them, not counted: the frame diff in (2) stops at the first heartbeat, so this had been `count >= 4`, which two routers that both stayed open and both emitted some fourth data line of any content whatsoever would have passed together. Post-heartbeat delivery on a long-lived connection is the one thing this verdict speaks for and it was the one thing it did not look at. The unrecognised-line-kind check runs on the LATE stream too; it had run on only one of the two streams this lane reads. WHAT IS NOT COMPARED: the stream's end, because a stream that ends has failed; and ordering between two subscribers under concurrent callers, which is D-p3-c

THE ROW WAS BLOCKED ON AN ORACLE AND THE ORACLE IS NOT WHAT BLOCKED IT. Measured on main at 7babd97, same request at both binaries: Swift answered 502 "registry search is unavailable: no HTTP client is configured" where the reference answered 200. RouterServiceDispatch built the daemon ControlDeps with no registry:, and NO production type conformed to HTTPFetching anywhere in app/Sources - every conformance lived in a test target. The merge, the dedupe, the limit coercion and the ranking were all implemented, unit-tested, and unreachable in the process that ships; a row blocked for an oracle reason reads as "probably fine, unmeasurable", which is why this was worth finding. P3 supplies RegistryHTTPClient and wires it. THE ORACLE is scripts/fixtures/registry-fixture-server.mjs on loopback, pointed at by MCP_ROUTER_REGISTRY/MCP_ROUTER_SMITHERY on both binaries, plus an in-TTL github-cache.json seeded into both homes so the GitHub enrichment - whose host is hard-coded in the reference with no env seam - is a cache hit rather than a network call, and the seeded star count is load-bearing for the ORDER of two rows so a cache that silently missed on both sides changes the bytes instead of passing. TWELVE scenarios diffed as RAW BYTES with NO normalisation, status compared alongside body: the envelope, the deduped source="both" row, both official install recipes, the four limit-coercion edges (0 and NaN to 30, the 60 cap, a negative reaching slice), an absent q, EITHER index answering 503 (both directions - only the smithery half was compared at first, so a port mishandling an official 503 specifically stayed green), the registry gone entirely, and both bases SET AND EMPTY, which is the nullish-default divergence RouterServiceDispatch calls load-bearing and which no scenario could previously see. Two assertions are ABSOLUTE rather than cross-router, because two routers that are equally wrong diff clean: the ranked order useCount->stars->updatedAt is asserted per router against an expected sequence the merge order does not produce, and a negative limit must return strictly fewer results than limit=30 on EACH router, since the echo proves only what was SENT and leaves a port free to slice locally afterwards. THE 60 CAP IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS: the corpus is 8 merged rows, so slice(0,30) and slice(0,60) return the same rows and only the fixture's echo of the received query string can see the cap at all - the forwarded limit is compared, the slice length at 60 is not. A shape guard refuses the run unless BOTH routers' own bodies carry every path the lane claims to compare, because two parsers that both returned nothing diff clean. RESULTS ARE BUFFERED AND FLUSHED ONCE AT THE END: the lane used to append each verdict as it went, so a lane that died after the happy path left the row PROVEN on six oks with the failure paths never run - the exact failure this item exists to refuse, inside the lane written to refuse it. NOT ESTABLISHED: that this client works against the REAL indexes - TLS, redirects and request headers are URLSession's and are unexercised here (D-p3-e) - and a schema change at the real registries is invisible to this row (D-p3-a). ControlDiff is deliberately left with no client, so the control lane keeps printing its in-process 502 rather than putting a live registry call inside every gate run

NOT BLOCKED ON WORK AND NOT WAITING FOR ANYONE - this row is a standing exclusion and this note is the decision. The fixture group claim is REFERENCE CURRENCY: the recorded body is still what the reference emits. This recording is one moment of two live third-party indexes, so re-capturing it compares the reference transform AND whatever the registries happen to be serving that second, and the second term is not the port's. P3 built a pinned fixture registry and could therefore have re-recorded this body against it and diffed it green. THAT WAS REJECTED: over a pinned corpus the claim collapses to "the reference still transforms P3 own synthetic input the same way", which control-registry-search already compares on every gate run against the LIVE reference and the LIVE Swift router - so the flip would have bought a green row carrying no information the gate does not already carry, while destroying the only production-shaped registry sample the decode suite has (repository "https://github.com/", a real malformed value no synthetic corpus would invent). WHAT THAT COSTS, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN WAVED AWAY: this row is NOT replaced by control-registry-search. The live-index currency claim - the reference or the client meeting a shape the registries no longer send - is carried by NOTHING, and that is D-p3-a; both parsers can mis-read a renamed field identically and every P3 row stays green. What HAS been recovered is the specific deformity: the owner-less repository "https://github.com/" is now served by the pinned fixture corpus as io.acme/ownerless and shape-guarded, so the nil-repoKey fallback to displayName is compared on the wire instead of sitting only in a fixture nothing diffs. CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: while this row is enumerated and unprovable, 83 of 83 is UNREACHABLE, so R4-C needs an owner decision on whether its target is 82 of 83 with this reason attached. The row is kept in the census rather than deleted, because deleting it would leave the numerator alone and shrink the denominator, and the coverage figure would RISE

dynamic client registration. Five refusals diffed byte for byte — a remote https redirect_uri, no redirect_uris at all, a cross-origin Origin, Origin: null, and a text/plain JSON-CSRF body — plus, per router, that a loopback registration returns a client_id and that re-registering the same URIs is IDEMPOTENT. That last one is not cosmetic: a client_id that changes per attempt is how an in-memory AS ends up answering invalid_client after a restart, which some clients read as logged-out and stop sending tools

the consent page and the code leg. Compared byte for byte: the refusal page for an unissued client_id. Asserted per router: the page renders 200, code_challenge_method=plain is REFUSED, a remote redirect_uri gets a 400 page and NO Location header, the page carries X-Frame-Options DENY and frame-ancestors 'none' and sets no CORS header, and POST /authorize redirects with a code echoing state. The 302's header set is diffed across routers — that comparison exists because the Swift 302 shipped with neither content-length nor chunking and never completed, while the Location header it carried was readable immediately, so every header-only assertion passed against a response that hung

four refusals diffed byte for byte — cross-origin, Origin: null, a forged refresh token, an unsupported grant, and GET. Per router: the code exchanges for an access and a refresh token, a WRONG PKCE verifier is refused, replaying the code is refused, the refresh token is accepted, and a refresh token minted BEFORE a restart still validates after it. That last is the statelessness invariant: tokens are HMAC blobs over one persisted 0600 key, and the lane checks the key's mode and its directory's

initialize carries an instructions field naming every upstream serving no tools. Member order is the reference's and was MEASURED rather than assumed: instructions goes last, after serverInfo. This surface reaches the model rather than the human, which is the whole reason it was chosen — a host injects it into the prompt, so "why can't you use X" gets answered instead of guessed

the four states, at both routers. Measured 2026-08-21 on the live router: 13 upstreams, 8 serving, and only two of the five silent ones are auth problems — auth.authorized reads true for FOUR of the five, so the tool count is the discriminator and that field is not. The lane asserts the never-authorised row names its upstream AND carries the command, and that a stdio upstream is told authorising will not help it. The case this row exists for is an upstream holding a valid refresh token and serving nothing: it must NOT be told to re-authorise, because that command cannot fix it

R15. Eleven routes — the six that predate this work and the five it adds — all answer 403 to a foreign Host at both routers. Before R15 the check lived inside the MCP transport, which the ladder reaches last, so /health, /status, /servers and /usage answered 200 to Host: evil.example while /mcp answered 403: a page on a rebound domain could read the usage history, the project list and every server's command line. envKeys is variable NAMES, so it was reconnaissance rather than a credential leak. The row also pins that /mcp's 403 body is unchanged byte for byte and that other routes get the ordinary error envelope instead of the JSON-RPC one. PROVEN BY P8, ON THE MUTATION AND NOT ON A SERIES, and the distinction is the whole history of this row. It was `proven` once on a term that agreed sixteen consecutive times and measured the wrong thing (D-p1-e), so what stands behind it now is the mutation harness `make parity-watch-mutations` runs, which runs the lane's OWN observation code (both it and this lane source parity-install-watch.sh, so the demonstration cannot drift from the thing demonstrated) and prints every arm with its denominator. It is named here WITHOUT its scripts/ path deliberately: parity-suite.sh executes every scripts/*.sh path a non-blocked note mentions, and at 27 trials against a 10s ThrottleInterval this one costs about 40 minutes - measured, because the first version of this note did carry the path and the gate duly ran the whole harness inside its suite lane (clean, which is a second independent 27-trial run and is why it is mentioned rather than hidden). Instrument-proving belongs where parity-lane-selftest already sits: out of the gate, dispatched by its own target. WHAT WAS BROKEN: `reran` was launchd's `runs` counter moving, and a counter that moved proves launchd SPAWNED the job - not that the job observed the change that was staged. THE FIX, IN TWO HALVES: (1) the staged change carries a STAMP, a server name neither binary can adopt, and both binaries write that name into their own watch.log - but only from a run that read a CHANGED file, because the hash fast path returns before any candidate is parsed (measured 2026-08-19 under a scratch HOME: the two log lines and the two watch-state.json hashes are byte-identical across node and Swift), so the term now asks whether a run OBSERVED this change; (2) the stimulus is delivered to the path the generated plist DECLARES, read back with plutil, instead of to a hard-wired $HOME/.claude.json - and the plist's path is REPORTED (`watched=self`, or the path) and never asserted, because a lane that reddens a mutation by noticing its own configuration is measuring the lane. MEASURED 2026-08-20, 27 trials on the Swift agent, each arm with its denominator: control 6 of 6 green on both terms; decoy (WatchPaths at a fresh `mktemp -d`) 6 of 6 RED, where the runs-only term it replaces would have been correct 0 of 6 - those agents re-ran eight times each (`runs=1->9`) and observed nothing; blind (HOME moved to a second, unchanging .claude.json with WatchPaths untouched, so launchd's deliveries are genuine and only the observation is missing) 6 of 6 RED with runs-only correct 0 of 6, which is the arm no series could ever have found; resident (`sh -c '<bin> watch; sleep 300'`) oneshot 3 of 3 red, so one term was not traded for the other. THE LANE ITSELF ran three consecutive pairs green, `stages=1/6` and a named stamp on all six observations. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, recorded because this row's history is a claim that outran its evidence: the `stamp-only` arm - half 2 reverted, which is P5's exact decoy - read `runs=1->1` in all six trials, not one spurious increment, where D-p1-e measured two in six on the same configuration. So it could not say whether the stamp ALONE would have sufficed, and the case for half 2 stays structural rather than measured: with it the decoy is red because the file the watcher reads never changes, which does not depend on a spurious-spawn rate at all - and that rate is now known to vary between sessions, which is itself the reason this row must not rest on a decoy that `usually` goes red. Nor does the term distinguish a launchd delivery from an unrelated spawn that read the same changed file; it does not need to, because a run that names the stamp has observed the change either way, which is what the installer's watch agent exists to do. EVERYTHING P5 BUILT IS KEPT: launchd's own `runs` counter, the settled predicate (`not running` AND an unmoved counter across a 3s window), the restaging loop that survives lossy WatchPaths delivery, and the evidence line - which now also carries `stages` with its denominator, the `stamp` that came back, and `watched`. Re-run `make parity-watch-mutations` after any change to either term.
